mole removal

Do you have any problems like this?

  • I'm worried about the mole on my face
  • I want to remove moles with laser
  • I want to use a scalpel to definitely remove the mole.
  • I'm worried about a mole, but I can't decide on a treatment.
  • I want to have a mole removed at a medical institution
  • Warts on my feet and fingers

How to remove warts and moles

Electric scalpel (mole)

This is a mole removal method using an electric scalpel called EK. Also called high-frequency electrolysis, it can remove raised moles and deep moles that cannot be removed with carbon dioxide lasers in one go.
Local anesthesia is required, but it takes about 1 to 2 minutes per mole, and as many as 10 to 20 moles can be removed in a short period of time.
Risks and complications such as redness and scarring may occur.

Excision suture method (mole)

This also uses a scalpel, but the difference is that the surrounding tissue, including the mole, is removed. After excision, the wound is closed with sutures.
Because it uses sutures, healing is faster than with the hollow-out method. It is also a treatment with a low risk of recurrence. Suitable for removing relatively large moles. However, since this treatment involves sewing the skin slightly, it is not suitable for cases where the surrounding skin may be pulled and cause problems.

Excision (skin tag)

Skin tags are warts that are approximately 1 to 3 mm in size and occur mainly around the neck, and are skin-colored to brown benign tumors.
If the tumor is small, we will cut it out with scissors, and if it is large, we will remove it with a scalpel.
The treatment method will be selected depending on the size and shape of the wart.
There will be a small wound after the removal, but it will close within a few days.

Side effects and downtime of mole removal

The side effects, risks, and downtime of mole removal are as follows.

Side effects/risks
  • After treatment, moles may come back.
  • The scar will remain red and hard for some time. It will take 3 to 6 months for it to completely return to normal.
  • In rare cases, pigmentation or depression may remain.
  • In rare cases, internal bleeding may occur.
Downtime and precautions

Treatment time: about 5 to 30 minutes
Downtime: 1-2 weeks *There are individual differences

  • If you use the hollow-out method, you will need to apply ointment and protect the area with tape for about two weeks.
  • If the excision suture method is used, it will be necessary to protect it with tape for a while. Please also refrain from strenuous exercise, drinking alcohol, taking long baths, saunas, etc. until the stitches are removed.
  • If skin cancer is found as a result of pathological examination, we will immediately refer you to a specialized medical institution.

tattoo removal

Do you have any problems like this?

  • I want to get my tattoo removed because I'm aiming for a job.
  • Now that we've decided to get married, before we start dating...
  • Considering the impact on children...
  • I feel inconvenienced by not being able to go to hot springs, pools, etc.
  • I want to erase a tattoo that reminds me of my ex-lover.
  • I was refused a life insurance policy.
  • I want to avoid social risks

Removal method using pico laser

At Norris Clinic, we perform tattoo removal using the medical skin laser "PicoWay" manufactured by American company Syneron Candela.
The high power allows tattoo removal to be done fewer times and in a shorter period of time than before. It is also highly effective in removing green and blue tattoos, which were previously difficult to remove.
In addition, PicoLaser has received pharmaceutical approval from the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare and approval from the FDA (U.S. Food and Drug Administration).

Side effects and downtime of tattoo removal

The side effects and downtime of pico laser tattoo removal are as follows:

Side effects/risks
  • Swelling immediately after irradiation
  • Scabs and blisters a few days after irradiation
  • Itching after 1 week of irradiation
Downtime and precautions

Treatment time: About 5 to 30 minutes (depending on the area)
Downtime: 1-10 days *There are individual differences

  • You can wash your face, put on makeup, shower, and bathe on the same day as long as you do not get the affected area wet.

Tattoo removal treatment process

1counseling

Staff and doctors will provide counseling. After checking the size of the tattoo, its color, and whether it is ink or ink, we will decide whether it is possible to treat it with pico laser.
We will also inform you of the cost, approximate number of treatments, and duration. If you have any concerns, please feel free to ask.

2anesthesia

A topical topical anesthetic will be applied.
If the area is extensive, local anesthesia via injection may be required.

3laser irradiation

The laser will be irradiated with the appropriate output.

4Post-irradiation treatment

After irradiation, a sensation of heat will occur. We will tell you how to cool your home and you can go home.

Precautions

  • Please refrain from bathing or sauna on the day of irradiation.
  • People who fall under the following conditions cannot undergo tattoo removal using pico laser. Thank you for your understanding.
  • Those who are pregnant, may become pregnant, or are breastfeeding
  • People with photosensitivity
  • Those who have just had an excessive sunburn
  • Those with severe inflammation or scars on the tattoo area
  • For those with true keloid

*People with atopic dermatitis or autoimmune diseases may not be able to undergo the treatment. Please consult with us first.

Side effects and risks

  • infection
  • Blisters
  • pigmentation
  • redness
  • Dye desorption
  • scab
  • scar (keloid)
